flawed_step: Lines 61–67 falsely claim that for each original arc (x,y), g(x,y)-f(x,y)=h(x,y)-h(y,x). This fails when G contains antiparallel original arcs, because both arcs contribute to the same two residual directions.
counterexample: Let G have vertices {s,t,u,v}, with arcs s→t of capacity 1 and u→v, v→u each of capacity 2. Define f(s,t)=0 and f(u,v)=f(v,u)=2. Define g(s,t)=1 and g(u,v)=g(v,u)=0. Both flows are feasible and conserved, with |g|=1>|f|=0. The construction assigns h(v,u)=2 from the original arc u→v and h(u,v)=2 from the original arc v→u. Hence, for original arc u→v, g(u,v)-f(u,v)=-2, while h(u,v)-h(v,u)=2-2=0, contradicting line 63.
assessment_summary: A concrete antiparallel-edge network falsifies an identity used to prove flow conservation, so the proof as written is invalid.
